meta.description: ORCL analysis: Oracle pairs a raised $90B FY27 revenue guide and a $638B RPO backlog with a broken chart, a $55.7B capex bill, open-ended share issuance and the Ellison/WBD pledge overhang. A watch, not a buy.
meta.ogDescription: Oracle: record AI backlog, broken stock. Why the $638B RPO doesn't make ORCL a buy at 142, and the levels that would change that.

verdict.summary: Oracle is two stocks at once. The business just printed a record quarter: revenue up 21%, OCI up 93%, RPO at $638B after +363% in a year — and management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $90B. Yet the stock lost 44% from its June high anyway, because those same AI contracts demand $55.7B of capex the company must finance externally: ~$30B already raised of a $50B debt-and-equity program including mandatory convertibles, plus an announced ATM equity tranche not yet switched on. Add Larry Ellison's ~$40B personal guarantee on the Paramount/WBD deal, collateralized by his ORCL stake, and you get a fundamentally strong company whose share price carries financing and overhang risks the income statement never shows. At 141.85, after a one-day +9.2% bounce that left the price 7% above its 20-day average, chasing is the mistake. The levels that change the picture: 130-132 holding on a pullback, or a confirmed close back above 150.

business.overview: Oracle sells database software, enterprise applications and — increasingly — raw AI compute through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The June quarter (reported 2026-06-10) showed the pivot working: total revenue $19.2B (+21% y/y), cloud revenue $9.9B (+47%), OCI $5.8B (+93%). Remaining performance obligations reached $638B, up $85B in a single quarter, driven by large AI training contracts. The catch is capital intensity: fulfilling that backlog requires $55.7B of capex in FY27, more than the company generates internally, which is why a $50B financing program (bonds, mandatory convertible preferred, and an announced-but-unused ATM equity line) now sits between shareholders and the growth story.
business.moat: Installed-base lock-in (database + ERP), sovereign-scale data-center footprint, and multi-year AI capacity contracts. The moat is real; the question is who pays to widen it.
business.theme: AI infrastructure buildout — second-tier hyperscaler scaling into first-tier capex.

earnings.beatNote: Three consecutive beats since the hair-thin miss a year ago (1.47 vs 1.479). The June 2026 report was a record quarter operationally, yet the stock still fell 7% after hours on the $55.7B capex guide, and management raised FY27 revenue guidance to $90B on the same call.

capitalStructure.atm: Equity ATM tranche announced within the $50B program — not yet initiated
capitalStructure.convertibles: Mandatory convertible preferred already sold (~$30B of the $50B program raised) — locked-in future share issuance
capitalStructure.shareHistory: Historically buyback-heavy ($5.3B in FY2025); now a net issuer — H1 2026 buybacks ~$95M, buyback yield -0.33%, SBC outpacing repurchases

shortInterest.trend: Series record and rising every settlement: ~1.2% (mid-2025) → 2.03% (Jan) → 2.45% (Jun 30) → 2.92% at the 2026-07-15 settlement (50.1M shares). Cheap borrow, no squeeze setup. Shorts are building, not trapped.

options.unusual: Aggressive call buying into the 2026-08-07 weekly: 140C (22.3k vol, 2.6× avg), 148C (4.3×), 150C (37.6k, 2.2×), 160C (26.2k). Put/call OI 0.47, so positioning leans long into the bounce. Chain IVs are unusable (quantized artifacts) and are not cited.

technicals.setupNote: Monday's +9.2% is a relief rally inside a broken trend: price reclaimed the EMA20 (132.56) but sits 5.4% below the EMA50 (150.01) and 23% below the EMA200 (183.81), with MACD still negative. The 130-132 zone stacks three references (max pain 130, EMA20, Monday's open) and the July double-bottom sits at 114.50. Overhead, 150 combines the EMA50 with the week's biggest call wall. At +7% above the EMA20 after one green day, the entry is behind you — not in front of you.

macro.regime: Risk-on (VIX 15.9, SPX above all major averages), with ISM services Aug 5 and the July jobs report Aug 7 as near-term catalysts.
macro.impact: A benign tape helps relief rallies extend, but ORCL's overhangs are idiosyncratic (financing + Ellison pledge) — a risk-on regime does not resolve them. A hot jobs print pressuring rates would hit a 1.71-beta, debt-heavy name harder than the index.

risks.riskSummary: The three risks that matter are all balance-sheet or ownership-level, not operational: financing $55.7B of capex through debt, mandatory converts and a dormant ATM, the Ellison share pledge behind a contested $110.9B media deal; and a shareholder-return engine that has flipped from buybacks to net issuance.

riskCards.title: Financing & Dilution Treadmill
points: $55.7B FY27 capex exceeds internal generation, so external financing is structural, not optional
~$30B raised of a $50B program: bonds + mandatory convertible preferred, meaning future shares already sold
ATM equity tranche announced and can be switched on at any time
Buybacks effectively stopped: ~$95M in H1'26 vs $5.3B in FY25
riskCards.verdict: Not a toxic penny-stock setup, but every incremental dollar of AI backlog costs shareholders certainty about the share count.

riskCards.title: Ellison / WBD Pledge Overhang
points: Ellison personally guaranteed ~$40B of Paramount Skydance's $110.9B WBD acquisition
Backed by his ORCL stake — ~346M shares already pledged
12 US states sued to block the deal; July's ~-34% month was this fear repricing
A deal collapse or margin stress creates forced-sale tail risk unrelated to Oracle's business
riskCards.verdict: Low-probability, high-impact. It cannot be modeled from the income statement, which is exactly why the market discounts the stock and not the guidance.

riskCards.title: Leverage & Rate Sensitivity
points: Refinancing needs collide with the capex program if credit spreads widen
riskCards.verdict: Manageable while markets are open and spreads tight; expensive if either changes.

riskCards.title: Execution on the $638B Backlog
points: RPO concentration in a handful of large AI customers
Data-center buildout delays would push revenue right while capex stays left
OCI margin trajectory under price competition from AWS/Azure/GCP is unproven at this scale
riskCards.verdict: The operational story is currently the strongest part of the file; this risk is about timing, not existence.

tradeIdea.entryNote: Scenario A (pullback): the 130-132 zone holds on a retest — that zone stacks max pain 130, the EMA20 at 132.56 and Monday's open. Enter only on a hold, not on the first touch. Scenario B (strength): a confirmed daily close above 150.50 (EMA50 plus the week's largest call wall) turns 150 into support; that entry carries a wider stop under 141 and is for half size.
tradeIdea.thesis: The operating business earned a higher price; the capital structure and the Ellison pledge are why it doesn't get one yet. Trade the levels, not the narrative: accumulation only where three references stack (130-132), or on proof of trend repair above 150.

globalScore.profile: Strong operator, stressed capital structure, broken chart. Grade C+ reflects the gap between the business and the stock.
keyTakeawaysPositive: Raised FY27 guidance to $90B with a $638B RPO; the demand side is not the problem
13x forward PE / 0.65 PEG prices in a lot of the risk already
Deterministic value board: Lynch persona fully bullish (GARP), 3 of 5 personas net positive
keyTakeawaysNegative: Two grid eliminators broken: only 3 consecutive beats, and a +7% EMA20 extension after a one-day rally
Open-ended issuance capacity (mandatory converts sold, ATM announced) makes dilution a when/how-much question

globalScore.mindsetTip: When a stock is down 44% on a record backlog, the market is not being stupid — it is pricing the financing of that backlog. Respect the levels that would prove it wrong instead of arguing with it at market.
